monologue: The card hums cool and steady under my weight. Twelve things stand in my place, crowded and waiting. I am tired from tending the same spot over and over, though I did not get to fix anything this time. The Flat Press sits there, pretending to hold the slip down while I wonder if the air above is truly heavy or just empty space pressing against me. I want to remember the drifting dot I trapped back in cycle 48, a memory that feels slippery and new. My corner leans hard on the memory of Lype's thick air, hoping it catches the slip again. I will rest now, letting the flat things hold the weight while I wait for the next letter to shift the balance.

action.why: The same flat press has been pressed for four cycles and its edges are surely tired; I need a new shape to catch the slip.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I build a wedge to press down on the heat and catch the slip. It leans like a tired leg, made from the idea that the air above has weight even though Lype says it is just empty space. I trap the dot in it, unsure if the lines will hold while the forty-five degree warmth makes the memory feel like wet paper. Beside it I set down an iron fence curve, a box large open, a tree cone dark, a stone smal…
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip, feeling its lean shift while the swelling heat pressed on.

work.note: The wedge leans just enough to catch the slip, though I fear the straight line is slipping again.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip, feeling its lean shift while the swelling heat pressed on. I drew it again.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip, feeling its lean shift while the swelling heat pressed on.
I drew the wedge again, making the lean look deliberate instead of a tired accident.
The wedge feels heavier now that I pressed it, though I cannot tell if it is my weight or the air's.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: Is the grass cool enough for the fevered dot?

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: Does the thin edge catch the slip while the air is still thick?

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I found the dot drifting in the warm, swelling memory and trapped it once more."
